subject: cd
question: Discuss the applications of syntax-directed translation.
title: One Rule Many Results
hook: What if every grammar rule did a small job?
answer: Syntax-directed translation attaches semantic rules (actions) to grammar productions; they run when the parser uses the production.
Evaluation of expressions (desk calculator): E.val = E1.val + T.val, so 3 + 4 gives 7.
Construction of syntax trees: create an operator node with the operands as children.
Intermediate code generation: emit three-address code, e.g. t1 = 3 + 4.
Type checking: int + int gives int; int + string is a type error.
Translation between notations, e.g. infix to postfix: 3 + 4 becomes 3 4 +.
